newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside project cost about A$1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Woodside project cost about A$1 bln.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said it will cost about A$1 billion to develop the Laminaria and Corralina oil fields in the Timor Sea, higher than the initial estimate of A$900 million but below the A$1.08 billion figure announced by the Australian government earlier on Monday.

The A$1.08 billion figure, referred to in a statement announcing the awarding of production license for the Timor Sea project by resources minister Warwick Parer, was based on a late 1996 estimate, a Woodside spokesman said. The estimate has since been revised down by Woodside, he said. "Since that time we've made some minor modifications," the spokesman said.

Woodside shares traded as much as 20 cents lower to A$9.45 by midday on Monday, although brokers said this was more related to a sharp fall in crude oil prices than concern about the project cost. The project is designed to produce 170,000 barrels of oil a day, with storage capacity of 1.4 million barrels.
Woodside owns 50 percent of the project. Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd and Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd hold equal 25 percent stakes.
